D: A drunk, grumpy superhero lets a PR man help fix his image, until a secret comes out.
P: Serve the mains when Hancock comes over for dinner at Ray's house.
S: Hancock throwing the beached whale back into the ocean
Prawns tossed in garlic, chilli, lime and melted butter, grilled 2 minutes a side until charred, piled high with lime wedges.
Ray's All Heart pitch to the big companies
Toasted baguette rubbed with garlic and piled with chopped ripe tomato, basil and good olive oil.
Prison yard toasted cheese and pickle
Hancock doing his time in prison

Sharp cheddar and tangy pickle toasted in buttered bread until golden and oozing, cut into squares and lined up on a canteen tray. Butter one side of 8 slices of bread. Lay 4 slices butter side down and spread each with 1 tbsp sweet pickle relish. Top with 200g grated vintage cheddar, then the remaining bread, butter side up. Cook in a frying pan over medium heat for 3 minutes a side, pressing down, until golden and melted. Cut each into 4 squares and line them up on a tray.
M: dinner with Ray, Mary and their son

Parmesan beef meatballs simmered in a slow tomato and basil sauce over spaghetti, with crisp garlic bread and a green salad. Mix 600g beef mince, 50g breadcrumbs, 40g parmesan, 1 egg, parsley and salt and roll 20 meatballs. Brown in olive oil. Soften 3 garlic cloves and 1 onion, add 2 cans crushed tomatoes and basil, simmer 20 minutes, then add the meatballs for 20 minutes more. Split a baguette, spread with 60g butter mashed with garlic and parsley and bake at 200C for 10 minutes. Cook 500g spaghetti and serve with salad leaves.
Ray giving Hancock a new public image
Sirloin steaks grilled to medium-rare and rested, with a cream and cracked peppercorn sauce, thick chips cooked twice and a green salad.
W: Hancock learning to say good job
Fudgy chocolate brownies baked at 170C for 25 minutes, cut into squares with a scoop of ice cream.
K: Whisky shaken hard with fresh lemon, sugar syrup and egg white until silky and foamy, poured over ice with bitters on top. For each drink, add 50ml whisky, 25ml fresh lemon juice, 15ml sugar syrup and half an egg white to a shaker. Shake hard without ice for 10 seconds, then add ice and shake again for 10 seconds. Strain into a short glass over fresh ice and shake 3 drops of bitters onto the foam. Make four, using 200ml whisky in total. For the sober version, make iced tea with lemon and honey.

s.note: Hancock throwing the beached whale back into the ocean
s.how: Toss 600g green prawns with crushed garlic, chopped red chilli, lime zest and melted butter. Grill for 2 minutes a side until charred. Pile high on a platter with lime wedges and pour over any butter left in the pan. Eat with your fingers.

s.note: Ray's All Heart pitch to the big companies
s.how: Slice 1 baguette and toast the slices. Dice 4 ripe tomatoes and mix with 1 crushed garlic clove, a handful of torn basil, 2 tbsp olive oil and salt. Rub the toasts with a cut garlic clove and pile the tomato on just before serving.

m.note: Ray giving Hancock a new public image
m.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thick chips and fry twice until crisp. Grill 4 sirloin steaks to medium-rare and rest. In the pan, toast cracked peppercorns, add 200ml cream and simmer until thick. Serve with the chips and a green salad.

w.note: Hancock learning to say good job
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour. Bake in a lined tin at 170C for 25 minutes. Cut into squares and serve each warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Good job.

Strain into a short glass over fresh ice and shake 3 drops of bitters onto the foam. Make four, using 200ml whisky in total. For the sober version, make iced tea with lemon and honey.
